items.stem: In an ASP.NET Core web app using OpenID Connect, which token is intended to prove the user's identity to the application?

options.rationale: Correct: the ID token carries authenticated identity claims about the user.
The access token authorizes calls to an API; it is not meant to identify the user to the app.
The refresh token only obtains new tokens; it carries no identity claims for the app.
The client secret authenticates the application to the provider, not the user.

items.explanation: Correct: the ID token carries authenticated identity claims about the user.

items.stem: Which TWO practices are recommended for an ASP.NET Core OpenID Connect web client? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use a confidential client with the authorization code flow and PKCE
options.rationale: Correct: this is the recommended flow for server-side web apps.

options.text: Store the client secret in Azure Key Vault or user secrets, not in appsettings checked into source control
options.rationale: Correct: secrets must be kept out of source control.

options.text: Use an implicit-flow public client for the web app
options.rationale: Public clients are no longer recommended for web applications.

options.text: Disable HTTPS to simplify local token exchange
options.rationale: TLS is required; disabling HTTPS exposes tokens.

items.explanation: Correct: a confidential code-flow client with PKCE, with secrets stored securely, is the recommended pattern.

items.stem: What is the recommended way to require authorization across a whole ASP.NET Core app while still allowing a few public pages?

options.text: Set a fallback authorization policy that requires an authenticated user and mark public pages with [AllowAnonymous]
options.rationale: Correct: a fallback policy secures everything by default; [AllowAnonymous] opts specific endpoints out.

options.text: Add [Authorize] to every single page individually
options.rationale: This is error-prone and easy to forget on a new page.

options.text: Check the user inside each action method manually
options.rationale: Manual checks duplicate logic and are easy to miss.

options.text: Rely on the OIDC provider to block unauthenticated requests
options.rationale: The provider authenticates; the app must still enforce authorization.

items.explanation: Correct: a fallback policy secures everything by default; [AllowAnonymous] opts specific endpoints out.
